ClusterName.description: Cluster name, unqualified — the stack prefixes it with the workspace. Renaming REPLACES the cluster: a new empty database, and the old one retained under the old name. Constraint: a lowercase letter followed by lowercase letters, digits or hyphens

DatabaseName.description: Initial database created inside the cluster. Postgres identifier rules: no hyphens. Constraint: a lowercase letter followed by lowercase letters, digits or underscores

MasterUsername.description: Master username. The password is GENERATED into Secrets Manager and never appears in this template, a parameter or a config file. "postgres" and "admin" are reserved by the engine. Constraint: a lowercase letter followed by lowercase letters, digits or underscores

MinCapacityAcu.description: Minimum Aurora Capacity Units. 0 lets the cluster pause when idle — cheapest, but the first connection after a pause waits roughly 15 seconds, which fails a health check that does not expect it. 0.5 is the lowest always-warm setting. CFN Type: Number, written as a string in the config (>= 0, <= 128).

MaxCapacityAcu.description: Maximum ACU. This is the cost ceiling and the only thing standing between a runaway query and a large bill. 1 ACU is about 2 GiB of memory with matching CPU. CFN Type: Number, written as a string in the config (>= 1, <= 128).

CreateReader.description: Add a reader instance in a second AZ. Doubles the cost. It is a read-scaling instance that also happens to shorten failover — Aurora survives an AZ loss without it, because storage is already replicated three ways.

BackupRetentionDays.description: Automated backup retention. Aurora keeps continuous backup for this window, so any second in it is restorable. Backup storage up to the cluster size is free. CFN Type: Number, written as a string in the config (>= 1, <= 35).

DeletionProtection.description: Blocks DeleteDBCluster at the API. Leave true for anything holding real data — it must be turned off in a separate stack update before a teardown can proceed, which is the point.

EngineVersion.description: Aurora PostgreSQL version. A major-version change is an in-place upgrade with downtime, not a replacement — test it against a restored snapshot first. Constraint: a major.minor Aurora PostgreSQL version, for example 16.4

VpcId.description: SSM path to the workspace VPC id.

PrivateSubnetIds.description: SSM path to the workspace private subnet list. Must span at least two availability zones — Aurora rejects a subnet group that does not, and the message names the subnet group rather than the cause.

KmsKeyArn.description: SSM path to the workspace CMK. Encrypts the cluster volume and the generated secret. Storage encryption cannot be turned on or off after creation.
